title: Polynomial-Time Composite Test
statement: For every bit string $z$, form the integer represented by the first component of its decoded pair. Define a Boolean test that returns true when this integer is less than $2$, false when it equals $2$, true when its least significant bit is $0$, and otherwise returns the negation of the conjunction of two liar-round tests, using respectively the length-sized prefix and the next length-sized block of the second component after appending three $1$ bits to the first component. The function sending $z$ to the singleton list containing this test result is computable by a deterministic finite-state Turing machine in time $C(n+1)^c$ on every input of length $n$, for some natural numbers $C$ and $c$.
caveat: The statement depends on the detailed definitions of the liar-round test and the bit-string pairing operations; the supplied descriptions do not fully specify the liar-round test.
